Subject: Initial: DPA carve-out question re: backups & restore

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the call yesterday — Stratus is excited to continue the procurement flow. Legal had one clarifying point on the DPA draft your team shared: they want to confirm the scope of the backup/DR carve-out language. Specifically: if Redwood retains encrypted backups for 90 days for operational restore, can you confirm (a) whether those backups could be restored into a staging environment in a third-party region for recovery testing, and (b) what subprocessors (if any) would ever have access to backup material during a restore?

Can you loop in whoever manages the DPA redlines and the SOC/Security evidence? We need this resolved before we push the DocuSign envelope to procurement.

Best,
Elena Ortiz
Sr. Contracts Manager
StratusHealth

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 9 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial: DPA carve-out question re: backups & restore

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear note. Looping in Neha (Legal) and Marissa (AE) to confirm. Quick answers up-front:

- Backups: Redwood retains encrypted backups for up to 90 days (operational need). Restores for customer-initiated failures are performed into the same customer tenant/region wherever possible.
- Test restores: We do run occasional restore drills; those are performed in isolated staging environments and are never used to serve live traffic. We can commit to doing drills in the same geographic region for Stratus if cross-border handling is a concern.
- Subprocessors: the only subprocessors that interact with backup data during restores are our managed storage provider (StorageCo) and the infra ops partner (CloudOpsInc). Both are under NDA and SOC2-covered contract clauses.

Neha — can you weigh in on whether Redwood can live with Stratus' suggested text that limits restores to the original region and requires prior written consent for any cross-border restore? I've attached the current redline for context (pdf excerpt).

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOC2-TypeII-Audit-Excerpt.pdf
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@stratushealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 10:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial: DPA carve-out question re: backups & restore

Hi Elena / team — thanks for raising this. I reviewed the Stratus suggested language and proposed a compromise in the attached redline (Stratus_DPA_v3_redlines.docx). Summary of our position:

- We can accept a clause that restricts routine restores to the customers region.
- For emergency restores that would require cross-border processing (e.g., region-level outage), Redwood requests a limited exception that allows us to restore into a secure, ephemeral staging environment in another region strictly for recovery purposes, with the following safeguards:
  * Data remains encrypted at rest and in transit; keys are controlled by Redwood unless customer uses BYOK.
  * Access limited to named operations personnel; access logs retained and provided on request.
  * Any cross-border restore must be reported to Stratus within 24 hours and documented in the incident report.

- Regarding subprocessors: we will provide an operations roster (names, roles) and runbook excerpts under NDA; we cannot broadly enumerate temporary contractors but will disclose subprocessors that could touch backups.

If Stratus is comfortable with the emergency-restore carve-in with those controls, we can proceed to DocuSign. If not, we can agree on a workflow requiring pre-approval for each cross-border restore.

Neha Kapoor
Sr. Counsel, Data Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Stratus_DPA_v3_redlines.docx

Subject: Re: Initial: DPA carve-out question re: backups & restore

Neha — thanks for the thoughtful compromise and for the safeguards. Internal legal reviewed your redline and can accept the emergency-restore exception with the controls you described, subject to two small additions:

1) Add explicit requirement that prior to any cross-border restore Redwood will provide a one-page notification to Stratus Legal indicating impacted customer data classes and the reason for cross-border restore (can be delivered after the restore if an active incident prevents prior notice).
2) Insert a 90-day retention cap on backups of certain "sensitive data" classes unless otherwise agreed in writing (Stratus provided a list in the separate email).

We will mark up your docx and push the envelope via DocuSign once Marissa confirms commercial terms. Procurement is ready to run DocuSign once final doc is attached.

Regards,
Elena Ortiz
Sr. Contracts Manager
StratusHealth
